description: ERECTION OF A NEW DETACHED DWELLINGHOUSE, CREATION OF NEW VEHICULAR ACCESS AND ONE OFF-STREET PARKING SPACE.
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - By reason of its combined siting, layout, bulk, massing, proximity to boundaries, the proposal results in an unsympathetic, cramped and contrived form of overdevelopment that fails to be in keeping with the character and appearance of the site and surrounding to the detriment of the visual amenity of the locality, contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan and Policy D12.3 of the Local Plan.

Reason : 2 - By reason of combined bulk, mass, height and proximity to the shared boundaries, the proposed dwelling would result in an visually obtrusive and dominant form of development to the detriment of the residential amenities nearby occupants, in particular, the occupiers of nos.80 and 82 The Drive, by way of loss of outlook, unreasonable sense of enclosure, loss of daylight and sunlight, overbearing form and loss of privacy contrary to, in particular, Policy D6 of the London Plan and Policies D12.2, D12.3 and D12.4 of the Local Plan.

Reason : 3 - By reason of the unacceptable layout, substandard internal ceiling height and poor quality private amenity space, the scheme represents over-intensification and over-development of the site that would result in sub-standard living conditions and environment to the detriment of the amenities of future occupiers.   Overall, the proposal would fail to comply with, in particular, London Plan 2021 Policy D6, Housing Design Standards London Plan Guidance 2023, Merton Local Plan 2024 Strategic Policy D12.1, Policies D12.3 and D12.4.

Reason : 4 - In the absence of a Flood Risk Assessment incorporating a drainage strategy, the proposed development has failed to demonstrate that the approach to the management of surface water flooding in critical drainage areas or measures to reduce the risk of surface water flooding would be acceptable, contrary to London Plan Policy SI 13 and Local Plan policy F15.8.

Reason : 5 - By reason of the scheme failing to achieve Zero Carbon and the absence of a legal agreement to secure the required carbon offset fund and in the absence of a detailed overhearting assessment (e.g. dynamic modelling against CIBSE TM59), the scheme fails to provide a sustainable and energy efficient scheme contrary to the aims and objectives of, in particular, policies CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3, CC2.4 and CC2.6 of Merton Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 5 - By reason of the scheme failing to achieve Zero Carbon and the absence of a legal agreement to secure the required carbon offset fund and in the absence of a detailed overhearting assessment (e.g. dynamic modelling against CIBSE TM59), the scheme fails to provide a sustainable and energy efficient scheme contrary to the aims and objectives of, in particular, policies CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3, CC2.4 and CC2.6 of Merton Local Plan 2024.

Reason : 6 - The application does not include details of Biodiversity Net Gain and In the absence of a s.106 legal agreement to secure the construction of the proposed development as self-build, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the scheme is exempt from Biodiversity Net Gain requirements, contrarty to the Environment Act 2021, The Biodiversity Gain Requirements (Exemptions) Regulations 2024 and Merton Local Plan Policy O15.3.

Reason : 6 - The application does not include details of Biodiversity Net Gain and In the absence of a s.106 legal agreement to secure the construction of the proposed development as self-build, the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the scheme is exempt from Biodiversity Net Gain requirements, contrarty to the Environment Act 2021, The Biodiversity Gain Requirements (Exemptions) Regulations 2024 and Merton Local Plan Policy O15.3.

Reason : 7 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did not engage in any pre-application discussions in relation to the creation of a new dwelling.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
